did_you_know.text: The name Bezalel is related to the words “in the shadow of God,” suggesting divine protection. The phrase “I have called him by name” emphasizes a personal and special appointment.
The verse lists several kinds of ability: wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and practical skill. The Torah thus connects deep insight with hands-on work.
The Tabernacle was not built by one person: Bezalel of Judah worked alongside Oholiab of Dan. This highlights the importance of cooperation among different people.
The Hebrew word kaporet is related to the root k-p-r, but here it refers to the cover of the Ark of the Testimony. Some translations call it the “mercy seat.”
The phrase “Sabbath of solemn rest” is an intensified expression, meaning complete or especially profound rest.

The verb vayinnafash is related to the word nefesh and is translated as “rested,” “was refreshed,” or “was restored.” It is a poetic description of ceasing from work, not a claim that God became tired.
